pattern.description: Live-action office shot over about 1.8 s: the standing colleague finishes walking out of frame right while the camera slowly tilts down and settles on the seated pair (deadpan 'Great.'). No graphics.
pattern.why_premium: A slow, motivated operator move with shallow depth of field and defocused foreground props gives the comedic reaction beat a cinematic finish instead of a static locked shot.

build_hint.gsap: No graphic build; footage plays as is. For a synthetic version on a still plate: gsap.fromTo(plate, {yPercent: -4}, {yPercent: 0, duration: 1.8, ease: 'sine.inOut'}) with the plate scaled to about 1.08 to hide edges.
build_hint.remotion: <OffthreadVideo> clip; synthetic version: translateY = interpolate(frame, [0, 54], [-28, 0], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.sin)}) on a 1.08-scaled still.

notes: camera.move is tilt_down (pan_y -0.18), so the move is reported as a camera tilt. The exiting colleague has no box of his own (he is gone by the end frame), so he is folded into the whole-frame b01. b02 (OCR 'M', mug/hand area) only shifts with the camera, so it is not listed. x168 is also reviewed in e028.
